title: Media render farm (FFmpeg)
description: An n8n workflow that turns one master video into every ad format and hook, renders them one at a time with FFmpeg, and checks every file before it is uploaded. Built by Dyaksa.
intro: An n8n workflow that turns one master video into every ad format and opening hook, renders them through FFmpeg one at a time, and checks each file against its spec before it is uploaded. Scroll to follow one variant through all 18 nodes.

stations.title: One request becomes every variant.
stations.body: A POST names a master file, the formats and the hooks. A Code node multiplies them into one job per variant, each with its target size, encoder settings and output path. An unknown ratio is skipped.

stations.title: The caller gets an answer before rendering starts.
stations.body: Respond to Webhook returns 202 with the number of queued variants straight away, so no client holds a connection open while a batch renders for minutes.

stations.title: Renders run one at a time, on purpose.
stations.body: Loop Over Items with a batch size of 1 means one FFmpeg process at a time, because encoding is CPU-bound. The encode is a reviewed shell script: it letterboxes instead of stretching, sets square pixels and normalises loudness.
check: Render One At A Time · batchSize 1 → render_variant.sh

stations.title: Done means checked, not “exited 0”.
stations.body: ffprobe reads every output and a Code node compares it with the requested spec. A file that is too short, too small, or the wrong width or height fails, even when FFmpeg reported success.

stations.title: One bad variant doesn't stop the batch.
stations.body: A failed render is logged to Failed Renders with the exact problem, #creative-ops is told, and the loop moves on to the next variant. Transcode and probe continue on error, so a crash arrives here as data, not as a stopped workflow.
check: Render OK? · false → Log Failed Render → Slack → loop

stations.title: Only verified files reach the manifest.
stations.body: A passing render gets a thumbnail, is read as binary and uploaded as multipart with Retry On Fail, three tries 5 seconds apart. Then it is written to the Asset Manifest as ready. The upload token comes from $env, never from node parameters.
check: Upload To Asset Store · retry 3 × 5 s

stations.title: One message per batch, not one per file.
stations.body: When the loop runs out of variants, Post Render Summary runs once and points the team to the manifest and the Failed Renders sheet.
check: Batch Complete? → Post Render Summary · execute once

stations.title: An unexpected crash still reaches a person.
stations.body: Anything the failure branch doesn't catch goes to an Error Trigger, which posts the failing node, the error and the execution link to #eng-alerts.

stations.title: 18 nodes and one loop.
stations.body: The loop is the queue: every variant, pass or fail, returns to Loop Over Items until none are left. The manifest it writes is what the DCO engine project tests against.
